Diamond Glue Co. v. United States Glue Co.
“A prohibition of the doing of business after a statute goes into effect is not retroactive with regard to that business, even though the business be done in pursuance of an earlier contract.”

"It is said that to grant the injunction prayed for in this case is to give the statute a retroactive effect. ... We give to the law no retroactive effect. ... Assuming such action to have been legal at the time the agreement was first entered into, the continuation of the agreement, after it had been declared to be illegal, becomes a violation of the act."
"Indeed, this does not give the proviso a retroactive operation. ... A statute is not made retroactive merely because it draws upon antecedent facts for its operation."

"Whether this application of the statute gives it a retroactive effect is the sole question here involved; and with that we find no difficulty. Under the statute the death of decedent is the event in respect of which the tax is laid. It is the existence of the joint tenancy at that time, and not its creation at an earlier date, which furnishes the basis for the tax."
“Thus the penalty was contingent upon an act which appellee committed not before but after the enactment of the statute, … and the penalty is incurred and becomes due on threshing.”
"A statute is not made retroactive merely because it draws upon antecedent facts for its operation."

“[T]he fact that the trackage contract was entered into in 1904 prior to the passage of the Act is immaterial; the provisions of the Act, including 1 (18), are applicable to contracts made before as well as after its enactment”
